----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Virendra Agrawal For Respondent(s) : Mr. D. K. Garg  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHUTOSH KUMAR  Order 18/07/2023 1.

The instant appeal has been filed by the appellant - Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation (for short 'RSRTC')
under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the judgment and award dated 03.07.2019 passed by Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Dholpur (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') in Claim Petition No.05/2019 whereby the learned Rajasthan State Road Transport ... vs Jardan S/O Chitra Singh ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95351922/
1
Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the claimant and awarded a sum of Rs.14,76,100/-.

2. Brief facts relevant for the present purposes are that on 08.06.2017 an FIR No.219/2017 was lodged in Police Station  (Downloaded on 11/11/2023 at 06:23:18 PM)
 [2023:RJ-JP:16732] (2 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019]
Kotwali, District Bharatpur stating therein that on 08.06.2017 the respondent No.1 - Jardan (hereinafter referred to as the 'claimant') along with his wife - Preeti and daughter - Kumari Gudiya had gone to Lodi Mata at Pipri to worship, on motorcycle being registration No.RJ-11-SJ-6826.

When they were returning and the motorcycle reached near Forest Department Crocodile Office, Sgarpada, a bus of RSRTC bearing registration No.RJ-11- PA-0311 came from the back side being driven at a high speed and negligently hit the motorcycle, due to which Preeti and Kumari Gudiya sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

3. A claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 was filed by the claimant, claiming Rs.40,00,000/- as compensation on account of death of Preeti and Rs.7,20,000/- as compensation for the death of Kumari Gudiya under various heads.
4. The claim petition was contested by the driver and the owner of the offending vehicle -RSRTC.

5. Learned Tribunal passed the impugned judgment and award Rajasthan State Road Transport ... vs Jardan S/O Chitra Singh ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95351922/
2 dated 03.07.2019 and partly allowed the claim petition and total compensation of Rs.14,76,100/- was awarded under various heads.

sentences.text: 6. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award of the learned Tribunal the present appeal has been filed to quash and set aside the judgment and award.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant - RSRTC submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed serious error in holding that  (Downloaded on 11/11/2023 at 06:23:18 PM)
 [2023:RJ-JP:16732] (3 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019]
accident in question occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the appellant - RSRTC in absence of any conclusive evidence.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant - RSRTC further submitted that the motorcycle on which the deceased were travelling was driven by Jardan, who is claimant himself and he was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and while overtaking the bus of RSRTC in rash and negligent manner he dashed the motorcycle against the bus and thus, the accident occurred.
Learned counsel also submitted that the claimant has not produced his driving license.

9. Learned counsel contended that the learned Tribunal has committed grave error by ignoring the fact that three persons were travelling on the motorcycle, which was in violation of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

It is difficult to balance the motorcycle with three persons and as such the accident in Rajasthan State Road Transport ... vs Jardan S/O Chitra Singh ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95351922/
3 question occurred.

sentences.text: 10. Learned counsel argued that the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased - Preeti, who was working as a tailor, as Rs.6240/- per month in absence of of any documentary evidence and there was no evidence regarding future prospect of the deceased.
To prove the age of the deceased - Preeti, no document was produced by the claimant.

11. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned judgment and award and argued that there is no force in the appeal hence,
it be dismissed.

12. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
13.

The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellant - RSRTC is that the accident in question occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the motorcycle and not by the driver of the bus of RSRTC.
14. In the considered opinion of this Court, the learned Tribunal has dealt with the issue of negligence on the part of driver of offending bus in right and true perspective and in detail.
The learned Tribunal has considered the statements of both of the witnesses i.e. AW.1 & AW.2.
They have deposed that driver of the offending bus brought the bus from the back side, drove the bus at a high speed and negligently hit the motorcycle of Jardan.
As a result of which Preeti and Kumari Gudiya sustained grievous injures.
They have also deposed that this accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of RSRTC.
A charge-sheet under Sections 279 and 304-A of IPC has been filed against the driver of the bus.
15. The documents annexed with the charge-sheet also supported the claimant's version of the accident.

The findings of the learned Tribunal, that the claimant was not at all negligent in driving his motorcycle and it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle alone, which caused the accident, is not liable to the interfered with.

16. The submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant - RSRTC that respondent No.1 - Jardan,
who was driving the motorcycle, has not produced his driving license and three [2023:RJ-JP:16732]
(5 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019] passengers were riding on the motorcycle, are not sustainable, as the Rajasthan State Road Transport ... vs Jardan S/O Chitra Singh ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95351922/
4 learned Tribunal has also considered these aspects of the matter in detail.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the motorcycle was being driven by the claimant - Jardan, and deceased - Preeti and Kumari Gudiya were sitting on the motorcycle and, therefore, no negligence can be attributed to the pillion riders.
17. So far as the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant regarding assessment of daily income of the deceased - Preeti is concerned
, the learned Tribunal, in absence of any proof of income of the deceased by doing the work of tailoring, has assessed her income to be Rs.260/- per day.
The learned Tribunal while assessing such income kept the deceased in the group of skilled labour.

18. The learned Tribunal while assessing monthly income of the deceased has taken into consideration that the deceased was worked for 24 days in a month only and assessed monthly income as Rs.6240/- (260 x 24).
19.

If the income of the deceased - Preeti is assessed as Rs.227/- per day as per the rate of daily wages prevalent on the date of accident keeping in mind that the deceased was a skilled labour, then the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.227 x 30 = Rs.6810/-.
Therefore, there is no much difference between the monthly income assessed by the learned Tribunal and by this Court.

20. Relying upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi & [2023:RJ-JP:16732] (6 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019] Ors reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the learned Tribunal has rightly enhanced 40% under the head of future prospects and looking to the age of the deceased as 27 years on the date of incident has rightly applied multiplier of 17.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi & [2023:RJ-JP:16732] (6 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was survived by her husband - Jardan only, therefore, under the head of personal expenses, the learned Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% of the assessed income of the deceased.
21. Under the conventional head, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.70,000/-.
It seems that learned Tribunal, for the death of deceased - Preeti, has not awarded the compensation on a very higher side.
Therefore, the findings of the learned Tribunal does not warrant any interference in this regard.

22. Taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and in the light of judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kishan Gopal & Anr. Vs. Lala & Ors : Civil Appeal No.7137/2013 and in the case of Lata Wadhwa & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors reported in (2001) 8 SCC 197 the learned Tribunal has granted fair and reasonable compensation to the claimant @ Rs.5,15,000/- due to death of Kumari Gudiya, which in the opinion of this Court is also not on higher side.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23. The learned Tribunal while deciding the issue Nos.1 to 4 elaborately discussed the evidence and awarded a 'just compensation'.
The findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal are based on legally sound reasoning, with which I fully concur.

[2023:RJ-JP:16732] (7 of 7) [CMA-4681/2019]

sentences.text: 5 24. The learned Tribunal has not committed any error in allowing the claim petition and awarded reasonable compensation to the claimant.
25. In view of the above discussions, this Court does not find any merit in this appeal, which deserves to be dismissed.
26. The present appeal is thus, dismissed.
27. Stay application and other pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of accordingly.
